study type: Secondary analysis of a cohort study
outcome: Composite neonatal morbidity (fetal or neonatal death, hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, respiratory distress syndrome, intraventricular hemorrhage grade 3 or 4, necrotizing enterocolitis, sepsis, birth injury, seizures, or ventilator use)
cohort: 52,162 singleton deliveries between 24 and 42 weeks of gestation
finding: Morbidly obese pregnant individuals had a 33% increased risk of composite neonatal morbidity compared to the reference group (normal/overweight BMI).
